name: Wendy Carlos
hook: Her Bach album sold the synthesizer to the public, and helped design the Moog it was played on.
blurb: Before 1968, most people had never heard a synthesizer. Wendy Carlos, who had worked with Robert Moog on the design of its modules, recorded pieces by Bach on a Moog modular, one line at a time, since the machine could only play one note at once. Switched-On Bach came out on Columbia in October 1968 and became one of the best-selling classical records ever. It matters to this map less for Bach than as proof: it showed a record company that a synthesizer record could sell, and sent a generation of musicians looking for Moogs. Later she scored Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange. Carlos is a transgender woman. The early pressings carried her former name, and the reissues carry Wendy Carlos. The map uses the name she uses.

signatureTracks.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 3, first movement
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From Switched-On Bach. Every string part played on one monophonic synthesizer, one pass at a time.
